topics.core_competency: The learner manages resources, evaluates their sustainability, and applies practices to improve food production efficiency.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: manage financial resources in meal planning and preparation for efficient food production operations. (u, s, v, gs)
manage time and energy in food production operations to ensure efficiency. (u, s, v, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In small groups, learners use textbooks and ICT resources to brainstorm the key financial concepts that can be applied to enhance efficiency in meal planning and preparation as they take note of the key points.
Learners in groups create a realistic budget that balances income and expenses for proper kitchen operations.
Learners analyse the risks and benefits of different financial choices made in relation to meal management as they take note of the important points.
Learners present in plenary

In pairs, learners use textbooks, and ICT resources to examine different time management techniques (e.g., batch cooking, mise en place — ‘everything in its place’ and meal preparation) used in food production as they take notes.
Learners create a time management plan for preparing elaborate meals. Note: They should justify the sequence of tasks and timing to ensure all dishes are ready for serving at a specified time.
Learners discuss strategies to minimise energy waste while maintaining food quality as they take note of key points.
Learners investigate the role of energy-efficient appliances (such as mixers, blenders, grinders, pressure cookers) in food production as they take note of key points.
Learners present findings in plenary.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: In a conversation, judge the learners’ ability to use key financial concepts to come up with a budget in meal management.
Observe learners during the presentation and look out for their ability to identify financial problems and way forward when budgeting for meals.
Evaluate the prepared budget for appropriateness and accuracy of figures.
Converse with learners as they formulate time management plans and look out for their ability to prepare an elaborate meal and manage time.
Observe learners as they create their time plans and look out for their ability to use imaginations to explore possibilities in meal preparation.
Evaluate the timed meal plans for their effectiveness in saving time and energy during meal preparation.

suggested_uses: Use textbooks and ICT resources to brainstorm key financial concepts
Use textbooks and ICT resources to examine different time management techniques

topic_metadata.topic_title: TOPIC 10: Bread, Cakes, Pastries and Confectioneries

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses the basic ingredients used in baking, modifies them, utilising their properties to achieve desired outcomes in the products.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: explore the different ingredients used in baking and to manipulate them to produce quality products. (u, s, v, gs)
explore the use of doughs, mixtures, pastries and batters in cookery to produce interesting products. (u, s, v, gs)
demonstrate advanced skills in making different yeast doughs, pastries cake mixture, batters and confectionery products. (u, s, v, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Collaboratively, learners use textbooks and ICT resources to examine the characteristics of various types of flour and their specific applications in recipes as they take note of the key points.
Learners discuss the importance and versatility of wheat flour in baking-gluten content.
They explore the milling processes of cereals— extraction rate of flours, identifying key steps and the significance of each stage as they take note of the key points.
Learners in groups examine the nutritive value of different types of flour (with different extraction rates) as they take note of the key points.
They investigate the best practices for storing flours to maintain their quality and freshness (factors such as temperature, humidity, and packaging), as they take note of the important findings.
Learners explore the uses of sugar, eggs, fat and raising agents in baking as they take note of important findings, and finally present in plenary.
In teams, learners use textbooks, recipe books, ICT resources (video clips) and any other materials to: a) analyse the differences between yeast doughs, pastries cake mixture and batters;

b) examine the manipulation (e.g., guidelines, qualities and faults that are likely to occur) of yeast doughs, pastries, cake mixture and batters to ensure proper consistency and texture of the products, as they take note of key points;
c) develop recipes that use yeast doughs, pastries, cake mixtures and batters as they take note of key points;
d) present in gallery.

Engaging with peers, learners leverage textbooks, recipe books and ICT (video) to: a) examine the different procedures of finishing (decorating), and presenting of yeast doughs, pastries cake mixture, batters and confectionery products; as they take note of the key points;

b) prepare and cook dishes using yeast doughs, pastries (e.g., pastry dishes with stuffing like meat and fish (for example, meat pies, cornish pasties, samosas, beef-roll, flan dishes, open tart, sausage roll, vegetable rolls; fruits dishes; pastry with cream; cheese), cake mixture and batter mixtures as they take note of the key points;
c) exhibit, critique and take videos of products.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Converse with learners as they discuss, judge their understanding of the characteristics of the various ingredients used in baked products.
Observe learners during their presentations to appraise their ability to plan, carry out investigations and evaluate different ingredients used in baked products.
Appraise their write-ups for accurate information on characteristics, nutritive value etc., of the ingredient used in baking.
Probe learners during the discussion as they develop recipes and appraise their ability to come up with interesting dishes.
Observe learners as they develop the recipes and look out for their ability to suggest and develop new solutions, and try out innovative alternatives.
Appraise the developed recipes for correct proportions of ingredients, accuracy of procedures and for creativity.
Engage with learners as they examine the methods of finishing baked products and appraise their ability to come up with suitable finishes.

Observe learners as they prepare the dishes and look out for their ability to: i) measure ingredients accurately; ii) use imaginations to explore possibilities in confectioneries and pastry; iii) try out innovative alternatives in preparing confectioneries; and iv) maintain hygiene throughout the production of dishes.
Appraise the dishes for texture, appearance, flavour, and taste.

practicals.title: Preparation of Yeast Doughs, Pastries, Cake Mixtures and Batters
practicals.description_verbatim: prepare and cook dishes using yeast doughs, pastries (e.g., pastry dishes with stuffing like meat and fish (for example, meat pies, cornish pasties, samosas, beef-roll, flan dishes, open tart, sausage roll, vegetable rolls; fruits dishes; pastry with cream; cheese), cake mixture and batter mixtures
practicals.safety_notes_verbatim: maintain hygiene throughout the production of dishes

suggested_uses: Use textbooks and ICT resources to examine the characteristics of various types of flour
Use textbooks, recipe books, ICT resources (video clips) to analyse differences between yeast doughs, pastries cake mixture and batters
Leverage textbooks, recipe books and ICT (video) to examine different procedures of finishing

topic_metadata.topic_title: TOPIC 11: Planning and Preparation of Meals (Part II)

topics.core_competency: The learner plans and prepares balanced meals efficiently while considering dietary needs to promote health and minimise wastage of resources.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: plan, prepare, cook and serve protein dishes for different occasions. (u, s, v, gs)
prepare, cook and serve suitable accompaniments for the different protein dishes to make balanced meals. (u, s, v, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners use recipe books, ICT resources and any other materials to write time plans for preparing, cooking and serving plant protein (beans, peas, nuts) dishes in different forms, with their suitable accompaniments (soups, sauces, carbohydrates (cereals, roots, tubers and plantain), vegetables, fruits and desserts) as they take note of the key points.

Learners watch video clips and use the experience to cook (using different methods), and serve red meat (beef, pork, goat meat, mutton, minced meat and offals) dishes with their suitable accompaniments (sauces, gravies and other hors d’oeuvres, carbohydrates, vegetables, fruits and desserts); as they take note of the key points.

Learners, in groups, use experiential learning to cook and serve poultry and rabbit dishes with their suitable accompaniments (sauces, gravies and other hors d’oeuvres, carbohydrates, vegetables, fruits and deserts); as they take note of the key points.

Learners cook and serve fish and textured vegetable protein (TVP) dishes with their suitable accompaniments (sauces, carbohydrates, vegetables, fruits and deserts); as they take note of the key points.
Learners exhibit the dishes.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Probe learners to ascertain: i) accuracy and orderliness of the time plans; ii) correct interpretation of recipes; iii) appropriate reasons for choice; iv) suitable combinations of dishes; and v) appropriate shopping lists/budget.

Observe learners as they prepare, cook, and serve the various dishes and evaluate their ability to: i) use imagination to explore possibilities in the interpretation of recipes; ii) try out innovative alternatives when combining dishes; iii) suggest and develop new solutions during the preparation of protein dishes; and iv) manage time.
Examine the dishes and look out for: i) appropriateness; ii) taste; iii) colour; iv) texture; v) readiness; and vi) presentation.

practicals.title: Cooking and Serving Plant Protein Dishes
practicals.description_verbatim: preparing, cooking and serving plant protein (beans, peas, nuts) dishes in different forms, with their suitable accompaniments

practicals.title: Cooking and Serving Red Meat Dishes
practicals.description_verbatim: cook (using different methods), and serve red meat (beef, pork, goat meat, mutton, minced meat and offals) dishes with their suitable accompaniments

practicals.title: Cooking and Serving Poultry and Rabbit Dishes
practicals.description_verbatim: cook and serve poultry and rabbit dishes with their suitable accompaniments

practicals.title: Cooking and Serving Fish and TVP Dishes
practicals.description_verbatim: cook and serve fish and textured vegetable protein (TVP) dishes with their suitable accompaniments

suggested_uses: Use recipe books, ICT resources to write time plans
Watch video clips and use the experience to cook

topic_metadata.topic_title: TOPIC 12: Réchauffé Dishes and Convenience Foods

topics.core_competency: The learner examines nutritional value of réchauffé dishes and convenience foods, uses them to prepare safe and nutritionally adequate dishes in order to reduce food waste and save time.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the importance of using leftover foods to create réchauffé dishes. (u, s, v, gs)
explore the use of convenience foods in food preparation. (u, s, v, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In small groups, learners use recipe books, ICT resources and any other materials to: a) examine the importance of using leftover foods to create interesting, nutritionally adequate dishes as they take note of the key points;
b) brainstorm the different left-over foods, guidelines and the suitable methods of cooking the réchauffé dishes as they take note of the key points;
c) assess the nutritive value of réchauffé dishes as they take note of the key points;
d) formulate a recipe for one réchauffé dish by creatively combining leftover foods as they take note of the key points;
e) demonstrate their skills in preparing and cooking different dishes using left over foods as they take note of the key points; and
f) exhibit their dishes.
In groups, learners use textbooks, ICT resources and other materials to: a) discuss the concept, types, advantages and disadvantages of convenience foods as they take note of the key points;
b) analyse the nutritive value and instructions of preparing convenience foods as they take note of key points;
c) demonstrate skills in using convenience foods to prepare, cook and serve interesting nutritionally adequate meals as they take the advantage of saving time;
d) take note of important points; and
e) exhibit and critique the dishes/meals.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Converse with learners as they manipulate the réchauffé dishes and look out for: i) nutritive value; ii) suitability of the preparation and cooking method; iii) adherence to guidelines of using leftover foods; and iv) conservation of nutrients.
Observe learners as they prepare and cook the réchauffé dishes and appraise the skill of creativity as they suggest and develop new solutions and try out innovative alternatives.
Evaluate the réchauffé dishes and look out for appropriateness, flavour, texture and presentation.

Converse with learners as they demonstrate skills in preparing convenience foods and look out for: i) the choice of the convenience foods; ii) the nutritive value of the dish/meal; iii) the suitability of the preparation and cooking method; and iv) time saving.
Observe learners during the preparation of the convenience food to judge their ability to manage goals and time.
Evaluate the convenience dishes for appropriateness, nutritive value, taste, colour, flavour, texture, accompaniments and presentation.

practicals.title: Preparation of Réchauffé Dishes
practicals.description_verbatim: demonstrate their skills in preparing and cooking different dishes using left over foods

practicals.title: Preparation of Convenience Foods
practicals.description_verbatim: demonstrate skills in using convenience foods to prepare, cook and serve interesting nutritionally adequate meals

suggested_uses: Use recipe books, ICT resources to examine the importance of using leftover foods
Use textbooks, ICT resources and other materials to discuss convenience foods

topic_metadata.topic_title: TOPIC 13: Food Safety, Processing and Preservation

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses sources of food contamination, explores different food processing methods, and applies effective preservation techniques to ensure food safety, quality, and extended shelf life.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: explore the principles and methods of food processing and preservation in relation to enhancing the shelf life of fresh foods. (u, s, v, gs)
process and preserve fruits, vegetables, pulses, nuts, spices and herbs to enhance shelf life. (u, s, v, gs)
apply processing and preservation techniques to produce enriched meat, fish, and poultry products to enhance shelf life. (u, s, v, gs)
process and preserve eggs and milk products to enrich their nutritional value, improve quality and extend shelf life. (u, s, v, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In small groups, learners use textbooks, ICT resources and other materials to: a) review the types and causes of food contamination, spoilage, and food poisoning;
b) examine safety practices for preventing food contamination, spoilage, and food poisoning as they take note of the key points.

c) analyse the methods (curing, smoking, freezing, canning and mincing) and principles (removal of air, application of heat, temperature control, moisture control, pH control, exclusion of micro-organisms and use of chemicals) of food processing and preservation of meat, cereals, vegetables, and fruits; as they take note of the key findings; and
d) present in plenary.

In small groups, learners use textbooks, recipe books, ICT resources and any other materials to demonstrate methods and techniques applied in processing and preservation of fruits, vegetables, pulses, nuts, spices, and herbs to maintain quality and extend shelf life as they take note of the key points.
Learners apply safe handling and storage techniques during food processing and preservation to prevent contamination as they take note of important points.
Learners establish the requirements for certifying products at a national level (UNBS), package, label and market the products.

In small groups, learners carry out a project by: i) conducting market research, to (define target customer segments, determine competitive pricing, develop effective promotion strategies, and identify optimal distribution channels for the products, packaging, labeling); and ii) exhibit and market all the products processed.
In small groups, learners use textbooks, recipe books, ICT resources and any other materials to apply various processing methods to enrich and preserve: i) meat; ii) fish; and iii) poultry.
Learners demonstrate food safety practices during the processing and preservation and take note of the key points.

In pairs, learners use textbooks, recipe books, ICT resources and any other materials to: a) apply various processing methods, to enrich and preserve eggs and milk—(cheese, ice cream, and yogurt, including curdling, fermentation, freezing).

b) demonstrate food safety practices during the processing and preservation (Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs) and Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP); package, label and market the processed products for sale as they take note of important points; and
c) exhibit in gallery.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Converse with learners as they discuss and look out for their ability to: i) identify safety practices for prevention of food contamination, spoilage and food poisoning; and ii) apply the methods and techniques used in food processing and preservation.

Observe learners as they present on types and causes of food contamination, spoilage and food poisoning; methods of processing and preservation. Judge their ability to: i) identify and explain the key concepts accurately and clearly; ii) communicate effectively using appropriate terminology and logical reasoning; iii) demonstrate critical thinking by proposing solutions to minimise contamination and spoilage; and iv) present coherently.
Evaluate the write-ups and look out for accuracy and coherence of information on types and causes of food contamination, spoilage and food poisoning and methods of processing and preservation.
Engage learners as they demonstrate skills and appraise their ability to process and preserve fruits, vegetables, pulses, nuts, spices and herbs.

Observe learners as they demonstrate and look out for their ability to: i) suggest and develop new solutions in improving shelf life of fruits, vegetables and pulses; ii) use imaginations to explore possibilities in processing and preserving of foods; and iii) safe handling and storage of food to prevent contamination.
Critique the processed products for texture, colour, moisture content, flavour, packaging, practice and labeling.
Probe learners as they process and preserve meat, fish, and poultry to judge their ability to enrich these products.

Observe learners as they demonstrate processing and preservation skills to evaluate their ability to: i) plan and carry out investigations in processing meat, fish, and poultry; ii) work with others to generate new ideas on processing and preserving meat, fish, and poultry; iii) try out innovative alternatives when processing and preserving meat, fish, and poultry; and iv) safely handle and store food to prevent contamination.
Appraise the enriched processed products for appropriateness, texture, flavour, colour packaging and labelling.
Dialogue with learners as they process and preserve eggs and milk to appraise their ability to enrich these products.

Observe learners as they demonstrate processing and preservation skills to evaluate their ability to: i) identify problems and way forward in enriching eggs and milk products; ii) plan and carry out investigations in processing and preserving eggs and enriching milk; iii) work with others to generate new ideas in processing and preserving eggs and milk; iv) try out innovative alternatives when processing and preserving eggs and milk; and v) safe handling and storage of food to prevent contamination.
Appraise the enriched processed products for appropriateness, texture, consistency, flavour, colour packaging and labelling.

practicals.title: Processing and Preservation of Fruits, Vegetables, Pulses, Nuts, Spices, and Herbs
practicals.description_verbatim: demonstrate methods and techniques applied in processing and preservation of fruits, vegetables, pulses, nuts, spices, and herbs to maintain quality and extend shelf life
practicals.safety_notes_verbatim: Learners apply safe handling and storage techniques during food processing and preservation to prevent contamination

practicals.title: Processing and Preservation of Meat, Fish, and Poultry
practicals.description_verbatim: apply various processing methods to enrich and preserve: i) meat; ii) fish; and iii) poultry
practicals.safety_notes_verbatim: Learners demonstrate food safety practices during the processing and preservation

practicals.title: Processing and Preservation of Eggs and Milk
practicals.description_verbatim: apply various processing methods, to enrich and preserve eggs and milk—(cheese, ice cream, and yogurt, including curdling, fermentation, freezing)
practicals.safety_notes_verbatim: demonstrate food safety practices during the processing and preservation (Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs) and Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP)

project_requirements.project_scope_verbatim: In small groups, learners carry out a project by: i) conducting market research, to (define target customer segments, determine competitive pricing, develop effective promotion strategies, and identify optimal distribution channels for the products, packaging, labeling); and ii) exhibit and market all the products processed.
project_requirements.deliverables_verbatim: exhibit and market all the products processed.

suggested_uses: Use textbooks, ICT resources and other materials to review types and causes of food contamination
Use textbooks, recipe books, ICT resources to demonstrate methods and techniques
Use textbooks, recipe books, ICT resources to apply various processing methods

topic_metadata.topic_title: TOPIC 14: Nutrition in the Different Stages of Life

topics.core_competency: The learner evaluates the nutritional needs in different stages of the life cycle, designs strategies that promote optimal health and development throughout the life cycle.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the nutritional needs of individuals at different stages of life to design suitable diet plans for them. (u, s, v, gs)
apply the knowledge of nutrition to support optimal health and development throughout the life cycle. (u, s, v, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Individually, the learner uses textbooks and ICT resources to: a) assess the nutritional needs of people at different stages of life cycle (pre pregnancy, pregnancy and lactation, infancy, infancy (exclusive breastfeeding & complementary feeding), childhood (toddlers, pre-school and school age), adolescence, adulthood and old age) as they note key points;
b) identify the nutritional challenges at each stage of life (listed above) as they take note of the key points;
c) examine the need for school feeding and identify strategies for promoting school feeding; and
d) present in plenary.

In pairs, learners use textbooks and ICT resources to: i) design meal plans for the different life stages, using nutritional guidelines, and justify how these plans support optimal health and development; and

ii) use the meal plans to create educational materials (For example, posters, brochures, or social media posts) addressing the importance of nutrition at different life stages as they take note of the key findings.
b) Learners present in plenary, during school events, local health fairs, or online platforms.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Dialogue with the learner during the assessment and evaluate his/her understanding of the nutritional requirements at the different stages of life.

Observe the learner as he/she presents nutritional needs and challenges at the different stages of life and look out for his/her ability to: i) reflect on his/her own experience and explain nutritional needs; and ii) comprehend the presentations.
Evaluate his/her write-up for accuracy of information on the nutritional needs and challenges of people at different stages of life.
Probe learners as they discuss and appraise their skill of developing meal plans that meet the nutritional requirement at the different stages of the life cycle.
Observe learners as they create meal plans and look out for their creativity as they work with others to generate new ideas for effective meal plans.
Appraise the meal plans to determine the extent to which they support optimal health and development.

suggested_uses: Use textbooks and ICT resources to assess nutritional needs
Use textbooks and ICT resources to design meal plans
Create educational materials (For example, posters, brochures, or social media posts)

topics.core_competency: The learner examines the food systems and environment, analyses the impact of food misinformation, and makes informed decisions about food choices to ensure healthier eating habits and food security.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the different food systems to ensure food security. (u, s, v, gs)
apply the knowledge of the food environment and design strategies to make adjustment which will ensure food security. (u, s, v, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs, learners use textbooks, ICT resources and any other resources to: a) investigate how cultural and geographical factors shape food systems in both urban and rural areas as they take note of important points;
b) evaluate the food blocks along the urban and rural food systems and present to the plenary;
c) examine the interactions between the stages of the food supply chain to enhance food and nutrition security as they take note of the key points;
d) Analyse the need to protect the environment for sustainability of the food supply; and
e) present in plenary.
In learning clusters, learners use textbooks, ICT resources and any other resources to: a) examine factors that influence the food environment (e.g., media, culture);
b) analyse the common types and sources of food misinformation and the groups of people that are vulnerable;
c) establish the reasons why such people are prone to food misinformation and come up with practical strategies to protect the vulnerable groups, as they take note of the key points; and
d) present in plenary.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Engage learners as they discuss and establish their understanding of how these differences influence local food traditions and consumption patterns.
Observe learners during the presentation to judge their ability to identify problems and come up with solutions in relation to the food systems.
Critique their write-ups for appropriate information about the factors that shape the food systems, food blocks and the supply chain.
Probe learners during the discussion and look out for their ability to come up with practical ways of protecting the vulnerable groups.
Observe learners as they present their findings and evaluate their ability to critically think, while developing the practical ways of helping the vulnerable groups.
Judge the write-ups for the effectiveness and suitability of the proposed practical strategies to protect the vulnerable groups.

suggested_uses: Use textbooks, ICT resources to investigate food systems
Use textbooks, ICT resources to examine food environment factors

topics.core_competency: The learner examines the role of nutrition in promoting optimal health and quality of life for individuals with different conditions and applies this knowledge to support their rehabilitation and recovery.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the different health conditions in order to design strategies that promote optimal health in rehabilitation and recovery. (u, s, v, gs)
apply diet and lifestyle practices that help in the management of health conditions, rehabilitation and recovery. (u, s, v, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In small groups, learners use textbooks, ICT resources and other materials to examine the interactions between three key elements of malnutrition, that is: the host (individual), agent (malnutrition causes), and environment (contextual factors) as they take note of key points.
Learners discuss the different health conditions that require nutrition management and rehabilitation.

Learners investigate the signs and symptoms of: metabolic disorders, malnutrition, injury and stress, and gastro-intestinal disorders, and others (e.g., Phenylketonuria (PKU), ulcers, burns, lactose intolerance, gluten intolerance/coeliac disease, colic diseases, diverticular diseases, hypertension, obesity, food allergies.)

Learners visit a health centre/watch video clips and other resources on malnutrition to investigate the types and levels of malnutrition in children in the community, and explore factors that contribute to malnutrition in children in the community, and examine the management practices for malnutrition.
Learners create a community action plan to raise awareness about prevention and management of malnutrition in the community by preparing brochures, leaflets and posters for sensitising the community.
Learners go out to the community to implement the sensitisation.
Learners write a report on the sensitisation.
In pairs, learners use textbooks and ICT resources to examine the importance of diet therapy in the management of metabolic disorders as they take note of important points.

Learners create a detailed care plan for individuals with a specific metabolic disorder, focusing on: i) nutritional needs; ii) dietary guidelines; and iii) lifestyle recommendations (Include a one-day sample meal plan customised for the disorder) as they take note of important points.
Learners present in plenary.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Engage with learners to evaluate their understanding of the concept of ecology of disease/injury.
Observe learners during the discussion on different health conditions and look out for collaboration, creativity and confidence as they articulate issues.

Critique learners’ advocacy messages and sensitisation session for: i) accuracy of messages; ii) communication skills; iii) confidence during presentation; and iv) appropriate information in the report.
Engage learners to establish their understanding of the nutrition requirements and dietary management of metabolic disorders.
Observe learners as they develop a care plan for an individual with a specific metabolic disorder, focusing on the clarity and effectiveness of their presentation.
Evaluate the learners' care plan based on the: i) accuracy of the guidelines for managing metabolic disorders; and ii) lifestyle recommendations.

project_requirements.project_scope_verbatim: Learners create a community action plan to raise awareness about prevention and management of malnutrition in the community by preparing brochures, leaflets and posters for sensitising the community. Learners go out to the community to implement the sensitisation.

suggested_uses: Use textbooks, ICT resources to examine interactions of malnutrition elements
Watch video clips and other resources on malnutrition
Use textbooks and ICT resources to examine importance of diet therapy
